member.name: T:Trimble.Connect.Data.Storage
member.summary: Detection and recovery procedures for V71-V76 corrupted storages. problem has been introduced in v2.3.17 when V70->V71 conversion has been implemented in a first place. The problem has been fixed in v2.4.7 that has schema version V76. So versions v2.3.17 - v2.4.6 are defective. The defect is related to 9 missed triggers. Current approach is to refuse to open the local storage when corruption is detected, ask user to recreate the storage from scratch and re-fetch the data. Normally this is not a big problem for user except additional time for initial sync, but we have a special case with local only storages than were never synced back to cloud. For local storages we do our best to recover all the data and data schema automatically on first opening of the storage. We utilize the fact that for local only storages effect of missing triggers is predictable and limited: 1. The hanging attachment link from todos/comments to not existing entities. 2. Files and folders that point to not existing folder as a parent. 3. There could be a Placements that is not attached to any file.
The storage state: key-value generic storage.
Persistent offline local data storage.
member.remarks: Instances of this class are not thread-safe and must be used from a single thread at a time. Each instance holds the SQLite database connection that is created when instance is constructed. If you need to access the same persistent storage from a different thread construct a new instance of the using copy constructor ().

member.name: M:Trimble.Connect.Data.SyncStrategy.IPullSingle`1.PullAsync(Trimble.Connect.Data.IRemoteStorage,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Pulls the specified entity or principal from the remote storage system.
member.param: The entity or principal identifier to pull.
member.returns: The entity's state in the remote storage system.
member.remarks: The entity state returned might be different from the local entity state after this method finished if there is a change conflict and local changes won. The merge logic applied in case of change conflicts is based on modification timestamp. The change (local or remote) with latest timestamp wins. The delete operation wins always regardless of timestamp. This method always pulls the latest state of the entity from the server and applies it to local storage. It does not use the sync cursor and does not update the sync cursor.

member.name: F:Trimble.Connect.Data.SyncableRepository`1.PushPullLock
member.summary: The lock for the duration of the any push operation: we should not allow pull operations while push is running because entity identifiers are assigned by server on push. If pull results are processed while waiting on push response it could happen that we receive result of the push as part of pull response then we cannot correlate the received entity with pushed entity, that cause the entity duplication in the local database with subsequent repeated push. - Ensures that only one operation is run in parallel. - The operation cannot be executed while global is running. - Serialize and operations. - Individual are not protected by lock, they are safe to do at any time.

member.name: F:Trimble.Connect.Data.SyncableRepository`1.ItemPushLock
member.summary: The lock to ensure the entity change pushed only once, but many push operations for different entities could run in parallel. See and .

summary.para: A key-value store on top of a file system with some extensions to support TC specific requirements: 1. The need for the stable identifier to refer to the file content to since identifiers are assigned by the server only after the push. This is solved by the content addressable storage (). We use a hash (MD5) of the content as a storage key. 2. Reduce the network traffic by allow sharing of the readonly file contents between apps and projects. 3. Some use cases to access blobs (ModelSharingFoundation) required the blob to be accessible as a file with a proper extension (e.g. .IFC). So storage must expose blobs as files with extension. 4. To support transformations (TC assimilation) for the blob content we allow to address blobs with compound key. The main key is shared between all blobs produced from the original content. The subkey allow to fetch the specific transformation for the original blob. To address the requirements above the blob storage uses a string pair as a key. Secondary key mapped directly to the file extension in the file system.

The file cache is two level. There is a local cache located next the project storage and a shared cache. On lookup the local cache has a precedence and overrides files in shared cache if any. When adding published files the shared cache should be preferred. When adding not published yet files they should be added to local cache and moved to shared cache after publishing. This way the shared cache is a real cache that can be cleaned up and restored from the cloud.
Location for the local cache is fixed: ".files" subfolder next to project storage. For the shared cache it is possible to override the location. E.g. user may prefer the D: drive or network drive.

member.name: F:Trimble.Connect.Data.Files.PushPullLock
member.summary: The lock for the duration of the any push operation: we should not allow pull operations while push is running because entity identifiers are assigned by server on push. If pull results are processed while waiting on push response it could happen that we receive result of the push as part of pull response then we cannot correlate the received entity with pushed entity, that cause the entity duplication in the local database with subsequent repeated push. - Ensures that only one operation is run in parallel. - The operation cannot be executed while global is running. - Serialize and operations. - Individual file and operations cannot be executed while is running. - At the same time individual files and operations can be executed in parallel.

member.name: M:Trimble.Connect.Data.IStorage.Clear(Trimble.Connect.Data.ClearOptions)
member.summary: Clear (purge) the local storage to free up the disk space. Depending on can remove all entities marked as deleted, all cached entities, file content.
member.param: The options to control what to clear.
member.remarks: This operation could fail is some entities cannot be purged because of e.g. link constraints. E.g. entity (e.g. file) cannot be deleted or purged if it is local only and attached to other entity.
